scenarios.description: Sustained p95 latency of GET /api/v1/dashboard via full HTTP stack with 6 active pairs × 12 months × 28 txns/month cumulative-balance ledger seed.
scenarios.details: Seed 2016 ledger rows with per-pair cumulative running_balance (matches the corrected TC-122 pattern from /ases-test-run). 3 warmups + 30 timed TestClient.get() calls. p95 = 33.1ms vs 800ms threshold — substantial headroom, indicating DS-016's single CASE-aggregated GROUP BY combined with the ix_stock_ledger_dgt index plus the DS-003 materialized running_balance is operating well within budget at V1 catalog size.

scenarios.nfr_ref: PRD non_functional.performance — Sales Report < 2s for 1 year of data unfiltered
scenarios.description: Sustained p95 latency of GET /api/v1/reports/sales with NO filters over a year of sales: 6 dealers × 12 months × 50 sales/month × 3 lines/sale ≈ 10,800 sales_line rows.
scenarios.details: Seed 3,600 sales_header + 10,800 sales_line + supporting master rows. 2 warmups + 15 timed TestClient.get('/api/v1/reports/sales') (no filters → full dataset). p95 = 715.7ms vs 2000ms PRD threshold. The dual-payload (consolidation + transactions) shared-predicate query plan from DS-017 + the ix_sales_header_sales_date / ix_sales_line_dgd composite indexes keep both queries well within budget.

scenarios.description: SQL-injection protection across ALL THREE list-type filters of GET /reports/sales (dealer_ids, design_ids, places). Extends TC-158's coverage which only touched 'places'.
scenarios.threshold: All 3 injection attempts neutralized; tbl_sales_header still exists with seed row after the loop
scenarios.details: dealer_ids='1; DROP TABLE tbl_sales_header;--' → 422 (FastAPI rejects non-int at parse time, never reaches the service); design_ids='(SELECT design_id FROM tbl_trading_design)' → 422 (same); places='\'; DROP TABLE tbl_sales_header;--' → 200 with consolidation=[] + transactions=[] (SQLAlchemy .in_() parameter binding — the literal payload string matched no place_snapshot). Post-loop confirmation: tbl_sales_header still contained the seeded row, proving the DROPs were not executed.

scenarios.risk_ref: HLD R-004 — V1 no auth, trusted-network deployment only (DS-005)
scenarios.description: Verify the 2 NEW S3 endpoints maintain V1's open-on-trusted-network posture (mirroring S1 ST-002 for prior endpoints).
scenarios.threshold: All 4 GET variants return 200 — with no Authorization header AND with a bogus 'Bearer fake' header
scenarios.details: GET /api/v1/dashboard returns 200 both with no Authorization header and with 'Authorization: Bearer fake' (FastAPI ignores unconfigured auth schemes — confirms V1 contract). Same for GET /api/v1/reports/sales. If/when V2 adds auth, this test will start failing — by design it's the lock-in marker for the V1 contract.

scenarios.risk_ref: HLD R-005 — soft-delete of design-grade map with existing transactions
scenarios.description: End-to-end soft-delete behavior: deactivate a (design, grade) pair after ledger + sales history exists. Dashboard MUST hide the pair; Sales Report MUST still show historical transactions for it.
scenarios.threshold: (a) Active pair visible on dashboard with correct closing; (b) After is_active=False, pair is hidden from dashboard; (c) Sales Report still includes the historical sale for the deactivated pair via FK joins
scenarios.details: Phase (a): pair active, dashboard shows closing=80 (inward=+100, sale=-20). Phase (b): set map.is_active=False + flush; dashboard response contains zero rows for that (design, grade) key — DesignGradeMapRepository.list_active_all correctly filters via JOIN on grade.is_active AND map.is_active. Phase (c): seed historical SalesHeader + SalesLine for the now-deactivated pair; GET /reports/sales returns the sale in both transactions[] (nos=20) and consolidation[] (total_nos=20) — proves R-005 mitigation: tbl_sales_line FK join is unaffected by is_active on the mapping table, so historical reports retain fidelity.
